fields.text: Our fieldwork catalogs variation in surface decoration on ceramic sherds recovered from six Bronze Age settlement sites, compared against regional museum collections.
The clinic's new appointment-scheduling software automatically emails patients a reminder and logs the time saved for the front-desk budget report.
We report a randomized trial comparing two dosing schedules of a lipid-lowering compound in 220 adult patients with elevated cholesterol, measuring LDL reduction at twelve weeks.

We describe the clinical course of a rare autoimmune skin condition in 40 patients, noting that most reported the condition's daily cost of managing flare-ups but offering no economic analysis of that burden.
We propose a new attention-sparsification method for transformer language models that cuts inference memory by 40 percent while matching baseline accuracy on three public benchmarks.

We design a constraint-based scheduling algorithm for operating-room time slots and show, in simulation, a 15 percent reduction in average patient wait time compared to the hospital's existing heuristic.
Using a difference-in-differences design across fourteen states, we estimate the effect of a minimum-wage increase on small-business employment over three years.

We build a simple rule-of-thumb forecasting procedure, described in one paragraph with no code or formal algorithm, to estimate quarterly retail sales, and evaluate it against a naive baseline using out-of-sample forecast error.
We train a convolutional neural network on whole-slide histopathology images to classify tumor subtypes, validated against pathologist annotations from 400 biopsy samples.
We develop a graph neural network that predicts protein-protein interactions from sequence data, and note in passing that faster discovery could eventually lower drug-development costs industry-wide.
We build a cost-effectiveness model comparing two diabetes treatment regimens, estimating quality-adjusted life years and total healthcare spending over a ten-year horizon.
We use a standard actuarial life-table approach, without any machine-learning component, to project the long-term healthcare costs and survival of patients starting a new hypertension therapy.
We develop a reinforcement-learning trading agent and backtest its portfolio-allocation strategy against historical market-index returns to measure risk-adjusted excess return.
We model investors as patient, boundedly rational agents in an agent-based market simulation, and compare the resulting price volatility against a reinforcement-learning trading baseline.
We combine a machine-learning model of hospital-readmission risk with a cost model to estimate the budget impact of a predictive discharge-planning algorithm across a regional hospital network.

We build a microsimulation that uses a trained classifier to flag high-risk diabetic patients for early intervention, and estimate the resulting change in total insurer spending under three policy scenarios.
We evaluate how a new drug-pricing regulation affects patients' out-of-pocket costs and manufacturers' research spending, using a structural model of pharmaceutical demand.

We propose a simple step-by-step rule, analogous to an algorithm, for a central bank to adjust interest rates in response to inflation, and evaluate its historical performance against discretionary policy.
We report unpublished interim results from an ongoing trial of a new anticoagulant in high-risk surgical patients.
We benchmark a proprietary high-frequency trading model against three competitor algorithms using a vendor's licensed intraday order-book dataset.
The symposium program committee finalized the schedule of poster sessions and assigned reviewers to monitor each session room.
The lab's new inventory-tracking app logs reagent stock levels and flags low supplies for the next purchase order.
We present a phase II trial of an inhaled bronchodilator in 150 adults with moderate asthma, reporting change in forced expiratory volume at eight weeks.
We summarize nursing-reported outcomes for 60 hospice patients, noting that families often raised concerns about the cost of at-home care, with no formal cost analysis performed in this study.
We introduce a quantization scheme for large language models that reduces model size by half with less than one point of accuracy loss on standard benchmarks.
We build a priority-queueing algorithm for emergency-room triage order and simulate its effect on average time-to-first-assessment, without modeling any clinical outcome.
We use an event-study design around a corporate-tax-rate change to estimate its effect on firms' capital investment over the following two years.
We tally, by hand with a spreadsheet and no predictive model, the historical frequency of supply disruptions reported by a regional distributor, and compare the counts across years.
We fine-tune a deep-learning model on retinal images to detect diabetic retinopathy, validated against ophthalmologist grades on an independent test set.
We build a natural-language-processing pipeline that extracts adverse-drug-event mentions from clinical notes, and note the pipeline could someday reduce the cost of manual chart review.
We estimate the lifetime medical cost and survival gain of a new hepatitis-C treatment regimen using a Markov cost-effectiveness model calibrated to trial data.
We compile a simple cost ledger, without any statistical or machine-learning model, comparing two wound-care supply regimens' total spend across a single hospital ward.
We train a gradient-boosted model to predict loan default and evaluate, in backtests, the change in a lender's expected losses under three underwriting policies.
We simulate a market of patient (slow-trading) and impatient (fast-trading) algorithmic agents and measure the resulting bid-ask spread under each population mix.
We combine a trained risk model for post-surgical complications with a hospital cost model to estimate the net savings of a new predictive-monitoring program across a hospital system.
We build a classifier that flags patients likely to skip follow-up appointments and estimate, under a simple budget model, the insurer savings from a targeted outreach algorithm.

We evaluate how a change in vaccine-procurement contracts affects national governments' negotiated unit prices and manufacturers' production investment, using a bargaining model of the vaccine market.

We describe a fixed, published step-by-step procedure, similar to an algorithm, that a finance ministry follows when revising its annual budget forecast, and compare its historical accuracy against discretionary revisions.
Internal draft notes summarize a funding panel's closed-door discussion of next year's research priorities.
We present not-yet-public cost and outcome data from a pharmaceutical co-funded diabetes-management trial, including unaudited financial figures.
We pair a machine-learning readmission-risk model with a cost-accounting framework to estimate the five-year budget effect of a hospital's new post-discharge nurse-call program.
We evaluate an unreleased internal fraud-detection model using the vendor's confidential production logs, which the data-sharing agreement does not permit disclosing externally.
